assessments.reasoning: json/details/OSL-3.0.json gives OSL-3.0, “Open Software License 3.0” and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Both reference fields list https://opensource.org/license/OSL-3.0 and https://web.archive.org/web/20120101081418/http://rosenlaw.com:80/OSL3.0.htm.
SPDX’s annotated v3.29.0 tag targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in the ordinary OSL-3.0 file URL. The repository reports an unsigned tag.
OSI record 406 has the ordinary OSL 3.0 notice and displays OSL-3.0. Its section 1(c) and title identify the edition to which the SPDX detail refers.

challenge.method: Checked the tag target, ID, title, deprecation, both reference routes and header against both OSI 3.0 publications.
challenge.results: The ID and notice identify ordinary OSL. SPDX records the OSI route as valid/live and the archived Rosen route as invalid/non-live. Neither link status changes membership, and the common version number supplies no basis to merge the entries.

limitations: The archive URL documents a reference route. Its target body was outside the scheduled originals. Legal equivalence, compatibility, general applicability and OSI approval are separate propositions.
reasoning: The release-pinned SPDX detail assigns OSL-3.0 to the ordinary Open Software License 3.0. Its standard header matches the notice in OSI record 406, which distinguishes it from the Non-Profit edition.
